speaker: Doctor
text:
The X-ray findings of dilated bowel segments with a gasless rectum, combined with the history of feeding difficulties and abdominal distension in an infant, are highly suggestive of Hirschsprung disease. I will now request a rectal biopsy to confirm the absence of ganglion cells.

REQUEST TEST: Rectal_Biopsy

speaker: Doctor
text: A normal rectal biopsy effectively rules out Hirschsprung disease, so I need to consider other causes for the obstruction and distension. Has there been any history of intussusception or umbilical hernias, and does the family have any history of cystic fibrosis?

speaker: Patient
text: The baby did not seem to pass stool normally and the belly swelling has become more obvious. Feeding has clearly decreased over the past few days.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the normal rectal biopsy, I need to rule out meconium ileus or other causes of distal obstruction. REQUEST TEST: Sweat_Cl_Test

speaker: Doctor
text:
With Hirschsprung disease and cystic fibrosis ruled out, I need to consider other structural anomalies like intestinal atresia or a malrotation. Has the baby had any episodes of bilious vomiting, and was the meconium passage delayed beyond the first 48 hours of life?

REQUEST TEST: Upper_GI_Series

speaker: Doctor
text:
A normal Upper GI series rules out malrotation and volvulus, which is reassuring but leaves us with an unresolved distal obstruction. Given the history of feeding difficulties, abdominal distension, and the X-ray findings of dilated bowel with a gasless rectum, I suspect an anorectal malformation or a distal stricture that may not have been fully evaluated by the previous tests. I will request a contrast enema to better visualize the distal colon and rectum.
